full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J : On an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act made by the Commissioner of Customs. Chittagong, a rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the delay ,0014 days in presenting the Customs appeal should not be condoned and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem tit and proper. 

 5. In reply, Mr Aminuddin, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 1 appearing with Mr Munshi Moniruzzaman submits that the Customs Act, 1969 (in short, the Act) is a special law and in section 194 D of the Act- special provision has been made for filing an appeal before the High Court Division within 90 days from date upon which the notice of order is received. He next submits that it has been clearly stated in the application for condo- nation of delay that the appellant received the order of the Tribunal on 22-10-2006 and therefore, there is no scope to file the appeal after 90 days from 22-10-2006. He lastly submits that section 5 of the Limitation Act is not applicable in a Custom Appeal as the said provision has not been made applicable in the Act and therefore, the rule is liable to be dis- charged. 

 6. Ms Kashefa Hossain, the learned Assistant Attorney General fails to show before us that there is any scope for condoning the delay of 314 days in presenting the Custom Appeal under section 5 of the Limitation Act. 

 8. It transpires that the provision of section 5 of the Limitation Act has not been made applicable in the Act. Therefore, there is no scope to condone the delay of 314 days in presenting a Custom Appeal by applying the provision of section 5 of the  Limitation Act. In the Act there is also no provision for condoning any delay by the High Court Division and to admit an appeal beyond the period of 90 days.
